_readme: Team-owned valuation assumptions. Edit a value, then run `npm run data` in app/. Every number here is a choice we must be able to defend; data-driven inputs (revenue, consensus, free cash flow, price, shares, net cash) come from Bloomberg and are NOT set here.

priceOverride.why: Team input, 24 Nov 2026; confirm and update on pitch morning. (Earlier: Google Finance $165.05 on 24 Nov; Bloomberg DES $135.46 on 20 Nov.) Keep research_market 'Share price' in app/scripts/research-data.ts the same.

wacc.why: Damodaran (NYU), US semiconductor industry average cost of capital, January 2026: 10.55%. Checked against Google Finance's rate for NVIDIA (14.45%, 24 Nov 2026) and Bloomberg's WACC (15.4%, Q3 2026); the slides show all three.

bloombergWacc.why: Bloomberg WACC, Q3 2026, confirmed by the team. Used instead of the 20 Nov 2026 Bloomberg WACC screen PDF, which showed 19.3%.

discountRates.why: The three rates the pitch shows: Damodaran US semiconductor average 10.55% (Jan 2026), Google Finance 14.45% (24 Nov 2026), Bloomberg 15.4% (Q3 2026). Nothing above 15.4% is shown to the board.

referenceOnly._note: Not shown to the board. Kept for our own reference.

terminalGrowth.why: Long-run growth after FY32 (%), roughly nominal world GDP growth.

fcfMarginYears.why: Base free-cash-flow margin = average of these actual years (Bloomberg).

position.why: Team choice: 3% of the portfolio, inside the 10% single-stock limit.

base.label: Base: analysts are right, then growth slows
base.why: FY28 revenue = Bloomberg consensus. Growth then fades in a straight line to terminal growth by FY32.

bull.label: Bull: consensus, with fatter margins
bull.why: Same revenue path as base; free-cash-flow margin 5 points higher (software and networking mix).

bear.label: Bear: rivals take share and spending pauses for a year
bear.why: A realistic downside: the build-out continues but custom chips and AMD take share, and customers digest their spending for a year (FY28 +10%, FY29 -5%, then recovery). Free-cash-flow margin 38.8% = NVIDIA's own FY27 year-to-date margin (docs/financials/AUDIT.md, Bloomberg), not an invented cut. Growth rates are the team's judgement, shaped like the FY23 pause and the FY20 dip.

stress.label: If AI ended for good: revenue flat, then down 20%, then no real growth
stress.why: Our harshest case, named 'If AI ended for good' on every slide: FY28 revenue flat on FY27, then a 20% fall in FY29, then 0% and 3% (no real growth) and long-run growth of 3% after FY32. Free-cash-flow margin 10 points lower. Harsher than anything in NVIDIA's history; a stress test, not a forecast.
